claim:tournelle-fleur-identity.statement: Domaine de la Tournelle Fleur de Savagnin is a distinct persistent wine from Domaine Labet's same-named wine; the producer describes it as 100% Savagnin from grey marl and deliberately ouillé/non-oxidative.

elevage.definition: The raising of a wine between fermentation and bottling: time, vessel, topping and other cellar choices all live inside it.
elevage.matters: Here it separates time in barrel from bottle age.

flor.definition: A film-forming yeast layer that develops on a wine's surface under the right cellar conditions.
flor.matters: It can shape aroma and structure more strongly than the grape name does.

marl.definition: A clay-rich calcareous rock or sediment; Jura growers often distinguish its bands, ages and colors.
marl.matters: It is useful site context, not a flavor guarantee.

mistelle.definition: A sweet wine made by adding spirit to grape must before or during early fermentation.
mistelle.matters: Macvin belongs to this family; it is not another name for vin jaune.

ouille.definition: Topped up: the barrel is refilled as wine evaporates, keeping headspace and oxygen contact low.
ouille.matters: It is the most useful word for avoiding the idea that every Jura white is oxidative.

sous-voile.definition: Under a yeast veil: wine ages without regular topping while a film-forming yeast layer develops on its surface.
sous-voile.matters: This is biological ageing, not simple neglect and not a grape flavor.

voile.definition: Literally ‘veil’: the film of yeast that can form over wine in a partly filled vessel.
voile.matters: The veil creates a biological pathway distinct from ordinary oxygen exposure.

projection_contract: Authored teaching copy is editorial, not Reference authority. Every factual tell, definition, lens, affinity, surprise, and recommendation carries governed claim IDs; every action resolves to a native subject.

affinities.reason: A documented close relative with tiny berries and unusually strong acid retention, living in a very different climate problem.

style_paths.name: {{term:sous-voile|Sous voile}}

person:emmanuel-houillon.thesis: Emmanuel Houillon's route into wine is unusually legible: apprenticeship in 1990, full-time work from 1997, and responsibility for the estate from 2001.

accent.intro: Jura has one of wine's most recognizable accents. The useful skill is not memorizing a flavor; it is learning which clues travel, why they work, and where they fail.

tells.clue: A strong clue because Savagnin is unusually central here.
tells.correction: The grape name does not tell you whether the wine was topped, raised under a veil, made sparkling, or headed toward vin jaune.
tells.title: Savagnin
tells.why: CIVJ reports Savagnin at 25% of Jura's grape distribution, and the region gives it several distinct cellar lives.

tells.clue: Walnut, spice and a {{term:voile|voile}} register can feel unmistakably Jura.
tells.correction: A topped Jura white may avoid that register completely. Region, grape and cellar method are three different answers.
tells.title: The oxygen clue
tells.why: CARTA documents both {{term:sous-voile|sous voile}} Chardonnay and deliberately {{term:ouille|ouillé}} Savagnin in the same regional world.

tells.clue: Pupillin is a village name that carries unusual recognition in wine culture.
tells.correction: It is a place and an appellation qualifier—not a producer, quality tier, or guarantee of one house style.
tells.title: Pupillin on the label
tells.why: The commune is a real production context near Arbois and the base associated with Maison Pierre Overnoy / Emmanuel Houillon.

accent.title: Recognizable. Never one-note.

lenses.text: Geographic AOPs, sparkling rules and {{term:mistelle|mistelle}} can occupy the same regional map while answering different legal questions.

place:jura.thesis: Jura has a strong accent because grape, place, law and cellar choice stay visibly entangled. Learn the tells—then learn why each one can mislead.

practice:ouillage.thesis: {{term:ouille|Ouillé}} means topped up. In Jura it is the word that keeps grape identity from being confused with an oxidative cellar path.

practice:sous-voile-aging.thesis: {{term:sous-voile|Sous voile}} is a biological ageing pathway under a yeast veil. It is not shorthand for every Jura white—or for simple oxidation.
